directive.quote: Port every behaviour and test; count old and new tests. Run the old code and the new tool on the same real input that is in git.

old_copy.deleted_with: the pull request in the source repository that removes the film's hold list once this tool is merged

preserve: a frame moves when it or a neighbour changed by more than the still level and no more than the cut level
a hold is a run of frames that neither move nor cut, timed by the frame rate, kept with the frame it starts on
holds are listed longest first (holds of one length in the order they start)
each hold is printed as <seconds>s@<start> with two decimals, two spaces between holds
allowed_deltas: the frames, the frame changes, the frame rate and the cut level come from this tool's own measure (read-data/measure-motion.mjs and motion-measure.json) instead of the place's installed motion tools
the video, seconds, still level and how many to list are flags; seconds and still level may be left out (all of the video, the still level read from it)
the answer is one JSON line: the holds as {seconds, at} and the old printed line as text
banned_substitutions: a still level or a bar written into the code

test_refs: tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/test/list-holds.test.mjs the longest hold comes first, each with the second it starts, and top keeps that many
tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/test/list-holds.test.mjs a still picture is one hold from its first frame, and a moving one has none
tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/test/list-holds.test.mjs the seconds asked for cut the video short, and a given still level is used
